answer: Texas uses electronic titles, so you won't need a paper title or a paper lien release. Instead, the lender sends the lien release to the state electronically. Ask your lender to release the lien; if you can't get that done, sign our lien release request, form NW-LRL-1, and we'll contact the lender for you, which can add 1 to 2 weeks. We can still make you an offer and book your appointment while you wait, and the title is transferred electronically at the appointment.
